standard_full: ASME B18.3 hexagon socket set screws, inch series. The pages used cite ASME B18.3-2003 / 2003 (R2008) (aftfasteners, globalfastener), B18.3-2012 (nickel-systems) or ASME B18.3 without an edition (deltafastener, packerfastener, fullerfasteners); badensteel and bayoucitybolt do not name the standard. All agree on every kept cell; cup and flat point diameter C is one column in the source tables; values compared between public manufacturer / distributor pages only, not checked against the standard itself

T_min 0.070: only 2 independent clusters (aftfasteners / deltafastener lineage; globalfastener + Fuller). The third vote in the researcher's count was fasten.it table 5A, whose own caption gives the unit as mm and which has duplicated / garbled rows - not counted. nickel-systems starts at #5, badensteel has no key-engagement column. With badensteel merged into the US lineage (shared deviant #1 socket size) C_max 0.061 and C_min 0.051 also have only 2 clusters. Values on the pages: J 0.050, T min 0.070, C 0.061 / 0.051.

checks: cup/flat point diameter max is 0.50 - 0.62 x thread diameter in every row
hex key size is 0.44 - 0.52 x thread diameter in every row
minimum key engagement >= key size in every row (equal from 1/4 up)
UNF thread count > UNC thread count in every row
every dimension column is non-decreasing with size; thread counts non-increasing
shape_hint: Headless fully threaded screw with a hexagon socket in one end face and a shaped point at the other (cup, flat, cone, oval or half dog). C is the diameter of the cup rim / flat face at the point; T is the minimum depth the hex key engages (valid for the longer standard lengths only).

role_map.C_max: cup and flat point diameter max
role_map.C_min: cup and flat point diameter min

notes: Researcher notes (written before verification; where they differ, the clusters field and the verification field prevail). Clusters: US-A = aftfasteners + deltafastener + packerfastener counted ONCE (AFT and Delta use the same non-standard letters K / F / D / H / S, Packer has AFT's row range); nickel-systems (own table, sizes 5 - 2, no #4), badensteel (C = hex socket, G = point diameter, from the drawing on the page; no key engagement), globalfastener 2003-edition cup-point page + fullerfasteners cup and flat pages (one Chinese template: dz cup = dp flat), fasten.it (table caption says mm, page title says inch series), bayoucitybolt (decimal socket size only), albanycountyfasteners (UNC count and key size, no #5 / 7/16). Thread counts additionally from general UNC/UNF charts. Column J for #4: every page that prints fractions for the larger keys prints the decimal 0.050 for #4, so the decimal is the designation there and decimal-only pages count for it. Tier B pages (eugenefast, mechcodex) are not counted; eugenefast prints 1/16 for #4-40. NOT used on purpose: boltport.com/standards/asme-b18.3/hexagon-socket-set-screws and globalfastener 'ASME B18.3 (T14 ...) 2012' pages reproduce the standard's notes verbatim (forbidden kind of source); torqbolt's ASME B18.3 set-screw page carries handbook / standard text almost verbatim (not counted); brightonbest, mscdirect, unbrako, americanfastener sheets are PDFs; zoro and boltdepot answer with a bot challenge. eicac.co.uk and screwboltsize.com print different key engagement / key sizes (different basis) and were not counted. T_min applies only to screws at least as long as the shortest-length column of the source tables (not carried here). Independence fingerprints: AFT and Delta agree in every shared column except Delta's typo at 1/2 (F min 0.70) and use the same letters -> one cluster; Nickel uses the J / T / C letters and its own size range; Baden its own letters with a drawing. The #4 row rests on exactly three clusters for T_min (US-A, globalfastener+Fuller, fasten.it) because the Nickel table starts at #5 and Baden has no key-engagement column. Left out although the numbers agree everywhere they appear: column J (fractional key size). Fractions are printed by US-A, Nickel and albanycountyfasteners; the last one has no #5 and no 7/16 row, so those two cells have two clusters. Keeping J instead would mean dropping the #5 and 7/16 rows (10 rows x 7 columns = 70 cells against 12 x 6 = 72). Verifier (2026-11-11, fresh downloads, own parser): row #4-40 removed (T_min had 2 clusters once fasten.it table 5A is not counted). Baden and bayoucitybolt are counted inside the AFT / Delta / Packer lineage, so every remaining dimension cell stands on exactly 3 clusters: US lineage, nickel-systems, globalfastener+Fuller.

verification.checks_done: Verifier (different from the researcher) re-downloaded on 2026-11-11 with curl + browser User-Agent every counted page, all HTTP 200: aftfasteners socket-set-screws page, deltafastener set-screw page, packerfastener set.html, nickel-systems set-screws/socket, badensteel socket-head-dimensions, globalfastener detail_1894, fullerfasteners cup-point and flat-point pages, fasten.it asme_b18.3_table_5a, bayoucitybolt, albanycountyfasteners, and the thread charts; eugenefast and mechcodex fetched only to confirm they are HTML, not counted. Tables re-read with the verifier's own parser (researcher's raw files and scripts not used); drawings on the Baden, AFT, Delta, globalfastener and fasten.it pages opened. Candidate 12 rows x 6 columns: #4-40 failed (T_min 2 clusters; C_max / C_min 2 clusters under the strict grouping) and was removed. Remaining 11 rows x 6 columns = 66 cells: J_in, T_min, C_max and C_min are each stated exactly by 3 clusters (US lineage aftfasteners + deltafastener + packerfastener + badensteel + bayoucitybolt / nickel-systems / globalfastener + Fuller); thread counts by 3 manufacturer / distributor clusters (+ albanycountyfasteners for UNC, + threadspec). Shared-typo test over all sizes each page lists (0 - 2): #1 hex socket 0.028 on AFT, Baden and bayoucitybolt against 0.035 on globalfastener, Fuller, Packer and fasten.it (shared deviation -> one cluster); Delta 1/2 C min 0.70, bayoucitybolt 5/8 0.3671 and six garbled fasten.it cells are not shared. Physical checks recomputed: C_max > C_min, C_max / d between 0.50 and 0.62, key size / d between 0.44 and 0.52, T_min >= key size, UNF > UNC, every dimension column non-decreasing. No PDF, document-sharing page, login page or page of standard text among the counted sources.
problems: Row #4-40 removed. T_min 0.070 is stated by aftfasteners + deltafastener (one lineage) and globalfastener + Fuller only; the researcher's third cluster was fasten.it table 5A, which is not counted (next item).

fasten.it asme_b18.3_table_5a not counted: the table's own caption says Dimensions in mm - source ASMJE B18.3 Table 5A while the numbers are inch values (the unit as stated on the page is wrong), sizes 5 and 6 appear twice with garbled cells, and at least six cells are corrupt (0297, 0.20, 0.27, 0.87, 0.141, 0.71). Its S / T / cup-flat values for #4 - 3/4 do agree with the record.

Independence of Baden and bayoucitybolt from the AFT lineage: in the set-screw table all three print 0.028 for the #1 hex socket where globalfastener, Fuller, Packer and fasten.it print 0.035 - a shared deviation, so they are counted as one cluster with AFT / Delta / Packer for this table (the researcher counted Baden and Bayou separately). Delta reuses AFT's set-screw drawing and letters K / F / D / H / S (already merged by the researcher).

Zero margin: after that merge every dimension cell of the 11 kept rows rests on exactly 3 clusters (US lineage, nickel-systems, globalfastener + Fuller). nickel-systems is counted separately for this table: own three-table layout with the ASME letters J / T / C, sizes 5 - 2, decimal and fractional key size, cites B18.3-2012; its flat / button tables do share AFT's layout, so the separation rests on the set-screw table alone.

Meaning of Baden's letters C and G comes from the dimension drawing on the page (C = hex socket, G = flat / cup point diameter); accepted as a legend. Baden is inside the US lineage here, so nothing depends on it.

J_in: aftfasteners, deltafastener, packerfastener and albanycountyfasteners print fractions from #5 up (same sizes, not counted as exact decimal matches); the decimal votes of the US lineage come from Baden and bayoucitybolt.

T_min is a conditional value: the source tables (AFT, Nickel) apply it only to screws at least as long as a per-size shortest nominal length that the record does not carry. The header meaning (minimum key engagement, hex socket) is stated on all three clusters.
Delta prints C min 0.70 for 1/2 (typo; AFT, Packer, Nickel, Baden, globalfastener, Fuller print 0.270).

Edition: nickel-systems cites ASME B18.3-2012, aftfasteners and globalfastener 2003 / 2003 (R2008); all agree on the kept cells. standard_full corrected; scope added because the table no longer starts at #4.
Not checked: the standard itself. The fractional J column stays dropped as in the researcher's record.
